policy_title: Ensure Access to Cash and Banking Hubs
stated: The Conservative Party will continue to ensure appropriate access to cash in local communities by requiring banks and building societies to consider customer needs when closing branches, building on the establishment of over 100 Banking Hubs.

source.quote: We have legislated to require banks and building societies considering closing a branch to consider the needs of all their customers and ensure they continue to have appropriate access to cash in their local community. We have already announced over 100 Banking Hubs...

bearing_set.reason: Cash access is a direct mechanism for affording essentials; its removal imposes real costs on cash-dependent households (ATM fees, inability to use cash-only services, financial exclusion for the unbanked), so preserving it has a non-negligible effect on real disposable income and payment access for lower-income and rural populations.

Older people are disproportionately reliant on cash and physical branches; banking hub provision materially affects their financial inclusion, with a concrete pathway to pensioner poverty indicators if access is lost.

Cash dependency is strongly correlated with lower income, older age, and disability; protecting in-person banking access disproportionately benefits those groups, narrowing the effective financial-services gap between richer and poorer households.

membership_note: The policy's primary material effects land on cost-of-living access for cash-reliant users (O2) and the distributional skew of those effects toward lower-income and elderly groups (O14). Effects on aggregate prosperity (O13) or community cohesion (O15) are too diffuse and mechanistically thin to clear the non-negligible bar.
